editor_note: None of the 7 rewritten entries changes the meaning. The trusted/untrusted condition in [20] and [25], the out-of-capacity and inaccessible-backend errors plus the low-capacity warning in [34], and the "one or more" jobs in [55] all match the English. editor_note: Entry 20 reverses the skip condition. The English says to skip to the next step if you are NOT in a trusted environment, meaning you are on a shared or public computer. The Korean '신뢰할 수 없는 환경에서 … 인증하는 것이 아니라면 [다음 단계로 건너뛰기]' says to skip UNLESS you are in an untrusted environment. That sends users on public machines to save_account(), which stores credentials locally, and sends trusted-machine users away from it. The other rewritten entries are faithful: entry 25 keeps the rotate/delete API-key caveat, entry 34 keeps the error-versus-warning split and suppress_low_usage_warning, and entry 43 renders 회로 트랜스파일, QPU 특성화 and 관측가능량(옵저버블) 역전파 correctly.

editor_note: None of the four rewritten entries (16, 33, 40, 56) would mislead a learner. Their meaning, caveats and quantities match the English. Entries 16 and 56 read naturally and need no change. Two naturalness slips remain. Entry 33 turns "Max-cut asks: … find a partition" into a command aimed at the reader ("…분할을 찾으세요"), where a problem definition ("…분할을 찾는 문제입니다") is expected, and its nested "정점들의 두 집합 S와 S̄로의 분할" is stiff. Entry 40 copies "the same object expected by the converters" word for word as "기대하는 것과 동일한 객체", when Korean API prose would say the converters take it as input ("입력으로 받는").

examples.source: Max-cut asks: given a graph $G=(V,E)$ with edge weights $w_{ij}$, find a partition of the vertices into two sets $S$ and $\bar{S}$ that maximizes the total weight of edges crossing the cut.

examples.suggested: Max-cut은 엣지 가중치가 $w_{ij}$인 그래프 $G=(V,E)$가 주어졌을 때, 정점을 두 집합 $S$와 $\bar{S}$로 나누어 컷을 가로지르는 엣지의 총 가중치가 최대가 되는 분할을 찾는 문제입니다.
examples.why: '묻습니다: …찾으세요' copies the English colon and ends with a command to the reader instead of defining the problem. The nested noun phrase is also stiff.

examples.why: '기대하는' copies the API sense of 'expected' word for word. Korean technical writing would say the converters take the object as input ('입력으로 받는').

editor_note: Entry 5 translates "first previewed at QDC 2025" as "ได้เปิดตัวครั้งแรกที่ QDC 2025", which reads as "first launched at QDC 2025". The same sentence already uses "ประกาศเปิดตัว" for the actual release, so the preview/release distinction gets blurred. Because "เปิดตัว" can also mean "unveil", this isn't misleading enough to fail, but "นำเสนอตัวอย่าง (preview) ครั้งแรก" would keep the distinction. In entry 11, "ต้องการ `qiskit-ibm-runtime`" is a calque of "require". A Thai technical writer would write "ต้องใช้". The meaning is otherwise faithful: beta status, both features, and version 0.47.0 or higher are all kept.

editor_note: None of the four rewritten entries (20, 25, 34, 43) would mislead a learner. Entry 20 keeps the trusted/untrusted condition and the skip-link logic, entry 25 keeps the caveat to change the API key after each use, and entry 43 renders QPU characterization well as การหาคุณลักษณะ QPU. The two slips are both in entry 34. It says "แสดง warning" and then "ระงับคำเตือนนี้" in the next sentence, so one warning gets two different words. It also renders the account usage "capacity" as ความจุ, which reads like storage volume. On top of that, "out of capacity" becomes มีความจุไม่พอ ("not enough"), which is a little softer than "none left".

examples.source: When capacity is low, `run()` emits a warning. Pass `suppress_low_usage_warning=True` to silence it.

editor_note: The rewritten entry 17 is accurate and does not mislead. All four capability bullets keep their meaning, and "Influence of regulations" is carried over literally as อิทธิพลของกฎระเบียบ, which keeps the same ambiguity as the English. Entry 21 keeps its meaning: the little-endian convention ("Qubit ที่มีหมายเลขต่ำที่สุดจะอยู่ขวาสุด"), the |00⟩→0 and |11⟩→1 outcomes, and the link to superposition all match the English. Entry 52 has one spelling problem. It writes "เกตควิบิตเดี่ยว", with the non-standard spelling ควิบิต, while the matching Z-gate line (entry 57) and the rest of the page's Thai prose use คิวบิต ("เกตคิวบิตเดี่ยว"). "เกต $X$" and "การดำเนินการ NOT" are correct and match entries 55-60.

editor_note: None of the six rewritten entries would mislead a learner. The crossover claim in [95] (unitary wins at short separation, dynamic wins at larger separation), the "not necessarily improved fidelity" caveat in [97] and the constant-versus-linear depth scaling in [99] all match the English. There are three wording problems. In [41], "entangling measurement" became "การวัดที่พัวพัน", which reads as a measurement that is itself entangled, not one that creates entanglement. In [97], "translate into fidelity gains" is calqued as "แปลเป็น", using the word for translating language, and "dominates" is calqued as "ครอบงำ". Also in [97], "today" is rendered literally as "ในวันนี้" where "ในปัจจุบัน" is more natural.

examples.translation: ทำไม fidelity อาจแย่กว่าในวันนี้: เวลา circuit ที่เพิ่มขึ้น ... มักจะครอบงำ

editor_note: Entry 5 is faithful and reads naturally in casual Taglish ("Excited kaming ianunsyo ang paglabas ng bagong `Executor` primitive ... na parehong unang na-preview sa QDC 2025"), and it keeps "new version," "helper class" and "both first previewed" without drift.

None of the 12 rewritten entries changes the meaning. The Strategy bullets in entry 17 (actionable insight, quantum-triggered na estratehiya, IP protection, Impluwensya ng mga regulasyon) match the English, and so do the headings. Entry 63 has a grammar slip: 'ang responsable quantum computing' is missing the linker. It should be 'responsableng quantum computing', the form entry 54's heading already uses. The accordion titles also mix 'pagpipilian' (entries 37 and 39) with 'pagpili' (entry 35 'Magagandang pagpili' and entry 33 'mapanganib o mahinang pagpili'). The word order in 'Mapanganib na mga pagpipilian' also reads a little stiff.

examples.source: Olivia Lanes explains that responsible quantum computing means maintaining an awareness of its power and potential impacts.
examples.translation: Ipinapaliwanag ni Olivia Lanes na ang responsable quantum computing ay nangangahulugan ng ...
examples.suggested: Ipinapaliwanag ni Olivia Lanes na ang responsableng quantum computing ay nangangahulugan ng ...
examples.why: The adjective is missing its -ng linker, which makes this ungrammatical. Entry 54 uses 'Responsableng Quantum Computing' correctly.

examples.source: Risky choices
examples.translation: Mapanganib na mga pagpipilian
examples.suggested: Mga mapanganib na pagpili
examples.why: The sibling titles use two different nouns: entry 35 has 'pagpili' and entries 37 and 39 have 'pagpipilian'. Entry 33 uses 'pagpili' for the same concept. The word order 'Mapanganib na mga' is also less natural than 'Mga mapanganib na'.

editor_note: Entries 21, 43 and 55 are faithful and read naturally. That covers the ε clipping caveat and the reduction to standard QAOA at ε = 0.5, and it covers the γ=0 identity argument ("ang cost unitary ay ang identity"). Entry 61 keeps its meaning but has two awkward spots. "gamit ang mas higit na kaunting iteration" stacks two comparatives ("more greater few") where it should say "far fewer iterations". "tumitigil sa paligid ng $-0.74$" puts "stops around" where the English says "settles around", which a native editor would smooth.

examples.source: converges quickly to near $-1.50$ (the exact optimum) with far fewer iterations
examples.translation: ay mabilis na nagko-converge sa malapit sa $-1.50$ (ang eksaktong optimum) gamit ang mas higit na kaunting iteration
examples.suggested: ay mabilis na nagko-converge malapit sa $-1.50$ (ang eksaktong optimum) sa mas kakaunting iteration
examples.why: 'mas higit na kaunti' stacks two comparatives and reads as a calque. The intended meaning (fewer) still gets across, but a native writer would not say it this way.

examples.source: settling around $-0.74$
examples.translation: na tumitigil sa paligid ng $-0.74$
examples.suggested: na nagse-settle sa humigit-kumulang $-0.74$
examples.why: 'tumitigil sa paligid ng' reads as physically stopping somewhere nearby. 'humigit-kumulang' is the natural way to give an approximate value, and 'nagse-settle' carries the sense of convergence.

editor_note: None of the three rewritten entries misleads a learner, but each one breaks a term convention the rest of the page uses. Entry 85 keeps the right meaning (account endpoint to discover values, functions endpoint to confirm the result) but calls the instance "екземпляру", while every other entry on the page uses "інстанс". The headings in entries 97 and 102 translate the product names as "Функції каталогу" and "Користувацькі функції", yet the sections under them (entries 98, 101 and 103, plus entry 87) keep "Catalog Functions" and "Custom Functions" in English. A reader who sees a Ukrainian heading over a section that uses the English name could briefly wonder whether they are the same thing.

examples.source: shows what a specific instance has already been granted
examples.translation: показує, що вже надано конкретному екземпляру
examples.suggested: показує, що вже надано конкретному інстансу
examples.why: Every other entry on the page renders 'instance' as 'інстанс' (e.g. entries 0, 4, 109, 114). Only this entry switches to 'екземпляр'.

examples.source: Catalog Functions {#catalog-functions}
examples.translation: Функції каталогу {#catalog-functions}
examples.suggested: Catalog Functions {#catalog-functions}
examples.why: The section right below it (entries 98 and 101) and entry 87 keep 'Catalog Functions' in English as a product name. The heading and its body should use the same form.

examples.source: Custom Functions {#custom-functions}
examples.translation: Користувацькі функції {#custom-functions}
examples.suggested: Custom Functions {#custom-functions}
examples.why: Entries 87 and 103 keep 'Custom Functions' in English, so the translated heading doesn't match the text under it.

editor_note: None of the three rewritten entries (15, 17, 68) would mislead a learner. They keep the source's facts: three of four NIST methods, the 2024 target, three signature schemes, z16 and IBM Cloud. They also keep the informal "ти" register, as in "Натисни". The remaining problems are wording. Entry 17 calques "quantum market information" as "квантову ринкову інформацію", which reads as if the information itself were quantum. It also stacks "Експертиза для ... для квантових технологій" and uses the clunky "ініціатив з інновацій". Entry 68 has the tautology "квантово-безпечних рішень безпеки", writes "пост-квантового" with a hyphen where Ukrainian writes "постквантового" as one word, and uses "впроваджувати ... у нашій інфраструктурі" where "у нашу інфраструктуру" is correct.

examples.source: Ability to convert quantum market information into actionable insights
examples.translation: Здатність перетворювати квантову ринкову інформацію на дієві висновки
examples.suggested: Здатність перетворювати інформацію про квантовий ринок на практичні висновки
examples.why: 'квантова ринкова інформація' reads as if the information itself is quantum; the source means information about the quantum market.

examples.source: Expertise to secure and protect Intellectual Property (IP) for quantum technologies.
examples.translation: Експертиза для забезпечення та захисту інтелектуальної власності (ІВ) для квантових технологій.
examples.suggested: Експертиза в забезпеченні та захисті інтелектуальної власності (ІВ) у сфері квантових технологій.
examples.why: The doubled 'для ... для' is calqued and stiff. 'ініціатив з інновацій' in the same list would also read better as 'інноваційних ініціатив'.

examples.source: quantum-safe security solutions
examples.translation: квантово-безпечних рішень безпеки
examples.suggested: квантово-безпечних рішень у сфері кібербезпеки
examples.why: 'безпечних ... безпеки' is a tautology that a native editor would remove.

examples.source: post-quantum cryptographic standard ... implementing them in our infrastructure
examples.translation: пост-квантового криптографічного стандарту ... впроваджувати їх у нашій інфраструктурі
examples.suggested: постквантового криптографічного стандарту ... впроваджувати їх у нашу інфраструктуру
examples.why: Ukrainian writes the prefix 'пост' together with the word (постквантовий). The verb впроваджувати takes 'у' + accusative (у нашу інфраструктуру).
